mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDPC1 (demand) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in FEDFUNDS above 4% triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods with FEDFUNDS >4% are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly growth in GDPC1 (demand) and INDPRO (supply) indicates robust economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly higher than baseline despite concurrent growth in both proxies (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained decline in UNRATE below 5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in late-cycle periods with UNRATE <5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor) and GDPC1 (demand) together signal strong employment and consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly higher than baseline despite concurrent rises in both proxies (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 7% triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods with UNRATE <7% are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO (supply) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) despite sustained supply growth.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained rise in FEDFUNDS above 4% predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods with FEDFUNDS >4% are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
